reason: The hypothesis makes specific claims about oxide formation, composition, and wear reduction in FeNiCrCoCu coatings, but no prior evidence is cited to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the specific oxidation and wear behavior of this high-entropy alloy under the stated conditions.
premises: FeNiCrCoCu forms a protective oxide scale rich in Cr and Cu oxides at high temperatures
This oxide scale reduces asperity contact and dissipates mechanical energy
Pre-oxidation treatment can deliberately promote this oxide layer
The oxide layer lowers wear rates compared to coatings without it
The mechanism applies to thin coatings on conventional metals at 600–800°C
